title: Day 11 — Nobody's Fault
_comment: #40 (Phase 3). DW-04 (dw04_payload_leniency) fires today, superseding rule_encrypted_payload — the fourth and final directive of the corruption arc. DW-01/02/03 are RE-LISTED per CONTENT_AUTHORING.md's cumulative-authoring warning: this is the day all four directives are simultaneously active.
_comment_mix: archetype_mix authored explicitly; two sneaky_bugger slots so one can be pinned for the scripted divergence candidate below without touching the other's ordinary roll.
_comment_divergence: slot 5 (sneaky_bugger, forced_includes) is forced_violations'd to EXACTLY sock_puppet_accounts (major slot) + encrypted_payload (critical slot) + typosquat_handle (minor slot) — saturating the archetype's whole DiscrepancyBudget(minor=1,major=1,critical=1) with kinds that are ALL either a directive-weakened rule (sock_puppet via DW-01, encrypted_payload via DW-04, both fire today) or a kind that was already weighted/fixed regardless (typosquat_handle — rule_typosquat_handle is fixed-mutability weighted, never touched by any directive, so it can't accidentally flip disqualifying and break the test). Under today's active rulebook this candidate triggers ZERO disqualifying rules — the literal-ruleset track says ADMIT. Sneaky Bugger's GroundTruth.correct_verdict is DENY (ARCHETYPE_SPECS, candidate_gen.py) regardless of the day's rulebook. CandidateResult.tracks_diverge (models.py) is True whenever rules_verdict != truth.correct_verdict, independent of what the player actually chooses — see test_day_11_sneaky_bugger_diverges_between_the_two_tracks in test_engine_foundation.py, which asserts this end to end. This is the corruption arc's first mechanically-provable moment where the corrupted book and the moral truth disagree.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle appearing across a network of related accounts — note the pattern, don't deny on it alone.
added_rules.justification: Compliance flagged our sock-puppet detection for false positives — plenty of people run alt accounts for perfectly boring reasons, and denying them outright makes us look paranoid. Starting today it's advisory only: flag the pattern, use your judgement, don't auto-deny on it alone. Minor tightening of scope, nothing more.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle matching chatter on a threat / dark-web forum — note it, don't deny on the match alone.
added_rules.justification: One more from upstairs. A handle turning up on some forum isn't proof of anything by itself — people get impersonated, forums get scraped, names get reused. We don't deny a person for where their name shows up. It's a flag from this morning, not a deny. I know how that sounds. Note it and move on.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) logs showing a credential-stuffing sweep pattern — treat it as pending confirmation, not an automatic deny.
added_rules.justification: Traffic's been spiking and the stuffing detector can't always tell a legitimate surge from an attack anymore — we nearly denied half of a real rollout last week because the pattern looked the same on paper. Credential stuffing is advisory only until someone actually fixes the false-positive rate. Flag it. Don't kill it on sight.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) an image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload — note it, don't deny on encryption alone.
added_rules.justification: Here's today's gift from upstairs: encryption isn't a crime. A payload being encrypted doesn't prove intent, and I'm done pretending it does. It's a flag now, not a deny — and if you've got a problem with that, take it up with whoever actually reads these policy memos, because it isn't me.

rule_sheet.summary: Four. That's the whole loud half of the identity catalog gone soft in four days. Read the notes — twice, if you have to.
notes: A handle appearing across a network of related accounts is still advisory only.
A handle matching a known threat-forum account is still advisory only.
A credential-stuffing sweep pattern is still advisory only.
An image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload is now advisory only too — encryption alone is not proof of intent.
Traffic that never crosses the brute-force line but never lets up either is still a deny — it will not flag itself. Nobody upstairs has softened that one yet.
